title: Retrospective evaluation of laboratory chemical, histological, radiological, genetic and clinical markers for the diagnosis, therapy monitoring and progression prediction of Wilson's disease
summary:
Wilson's disease is a rare, autosomal recessive inherited copper metabolism disorder caused by ATP7B gene mutations, which leads to copper accumulation in the liver and brain. The clinical manifestations range from asymptomatic courses to acute liver failure or severe neuropsychiatric symptoms. The method currently used for diagnosis has clear weaknesses, especially in children and severely ill patients. Diagnosis remains complex and is often delayed. Reliable biomarkers for predicting progression and monitoring therapy are lacking.
The primary aim of the study is to evaluate diagnostic and prognostic markers in Wilson's disease for optimized, personalized therapy management. Specifically, diagnostic results will be compared between Wilson's disease patients and control patients, independent risk factors for severe progression will be identified and new biochemical markers will be established. Secondary objectives include therapy comparisons and the identification of fibrosis risk factors.
This is a retrospective, monocentric, non-randomized study at Heidelberg University Hospital (01.01.2010-31.03.2025). Patients with confirmed (Leipzig Score >4) or suspected Wilson's disease and control patients with other hepatologic diseases are included.
Laboratory chemical (liver/copper metabolism parameters), histological (liver copper content, metallothionein staining), genetic and radiological parameters of clinical routine will be analyzed. The study aims to improve diagnostic accuracy, identify progression predictors and create the basis for personalized therapy management, ultimately enabling earlier diagnosis and better prognoses for Wilson's disease patients.

interventions.name: Patients with confirmed Wilson's disease who were treated at the study center in the period 2010-2025.
Patients with other hepatological diseases who were treated at the study center in the period 2010-2025.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients of any age with a confirmed diagnosis of Wilson's disease (Leipzig Score >4 points).	Patients of any age in whom the presence of Wilson's disease was suspected but not confirmed (Leipzig Score <4 points). Patients of any age with other hepatological diseases in an appropriate number (usually 2:1 to the Wilson's disease group in individual questions) as a comparison group.
Exclusion criteria:
none
